newsitem.title: DUBAI: India preparing child beggars to leave Saudi.
newsitem.headline: India preparing child beggars to leave Saudi.

text.p: India will give travel papers by Thursday to 46 children awaiting deportation from Saudi Arabia after being caught begging, Indian diplomats in the kingdom said on Tuesday.

The 40 boys and six girls, aged between six and 14, appeared to have entered Saudi Arabia, known for tough visa laws, as Moslem pilgrims in families. When relatives returned to India they stayed behind as beggers.

They were caught 10 days ago pleading for food and money in the streets of Mecca and Medina, home to two of Islam's holiest shrines, and were taken to the deportation centre in nearby Jeddah without identification papers.
The Indian consulate in Jeddah began issuing them papers after ensuring the youngsters were Indian nationals.

"By Thursday, all the issuing of certificates will be over as each document is granted after authorities provide us with photos of each of the children," an Indian diplomat told Reuters by telephone from Saudi Arabia.
He said diplomats visited the children and found them in "good condition". He would not say when they would leave Saudi Arabia, which will pay for their return air tickets.
"This is in the hands of the local authorities, but I expect it will follow soon after the process of issuing their papers is over," the diplomat said.

They would be the second batch of Indian children deported by Saudi Arabia in less than two weeks for staying illegally in the oil-rich country and earning their living as beggers. At least 76 girls aged between five and 14, many handicapped, were deported to Bombay on January 13.

Most came from Murshidbad in India's eastern state of West Bengal. Diplomats said Indian authorities began investigating after the first group left and suspicions were rife that an organised gang was involved.
"But until now, I have nothing official on the results of the Indian investigation to shed more light," said the Indian diplomat.
